name: Knorri (Hörri)
description: Knorri (also known as HÃ¶rri) is a traditional Finnish card game for three to eight players. It belongs to the 'beating' or 'avoidance' family of games (like Skitgubbe). The game is uniquely divided into two phases: a 'Collection Phase' where cards are picked up from the table based on rank-matching, and a 'Trick Phase' where players must play the cards they collected to avoid being the last person with cards in hand.

history.origins: Originates in Finland, likely derived from the Swedish game 'Mas' or 'Skitgubbe'. The name 'Knorri' is localized Finnish slang for the rhythmic flipping of cards.
timeline: Late 19th Century: Beating games gain popularity in the Nordic maritime trade routes.
1920s: Knorri becomes a distinct Finnish variant with the 'Diamonds-as-Trump' rule.
Present: Played in rural Finland and among traditional card game enthusiasts.
history.cultural: Commonly played as a social game where 'losing' is the main concern, rather than scoring high points.
history.evolution: Knorri preserved the 'Complete Information' aspect of early Nordic beating games, where all cards are visible during the first phase.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Diamonds are **Trumps**. Clubs are **Hard/Anti-Trump** (Anti-Truff).
setup.dealing: No cards are dealt to players. 9 cards are placed face-up on the table to start. The rest form a draw pile.

rules.objective: Avoid being the last player left with cards in your hand at the end of the second phase.

strategy.basic: In Phase 1, try to avoid cards that have many smaller cards of the same suit on the table. You want a small, manageable hand for the trick phase.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Club Shield': Since Clubs cannot be trumped by Diamonds, they are the safest cards to lead if you want to ensure a trick follows standard suit-ranking without interference.
strategy.advanced: Phase 1 Memory: Since you see every card entering the table/hands, remember who picked up the high Diamonds. Use your Clubs to neutralize their trump advantage during the second phase.
tips: In the first phase, if you must take a card, try to take one that completes a sequence (e.g., if you take a 10 and an 8 is on the table).
Save your Diamonds (Trumps) for the very end of the trick phase to secure your 'exit' from the game.

variations.name: Soft clubs
variations.description: Clubs can be beaten by any spade, heart or diamond; diamonds trump all, hearts and spades trump clubs, clubs beat only lower clubs.

variations.name: Scoring
variations.description: Optional scoring: +1 per player still in when you go out; loser gets negative points so total is zero (e.g. 4-player: +3, +2, +1, -6).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring is optional and cumulative; scoring overrides to be added when implementing.

variations.name: Last Card
variations.description: Player with one card must announce "last card" before next player plays; forgetting forces them to take bottom card of trick on next turn instead of going out.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule affects turn outcome only; no engine constant overrides needed.
